candidates.change_summary: Return _msgSender() instead of the stored _owner, so owner() returns the caller.
Return the zero address instead of the stored _owner.
Return msg.sender directly instead of the stored _owner.
Removed the _checkOwner() call so any caller (not just the owner) can invoke transferOwnership and change owner.
Removed the zero-address require so transferring ownership to address(0) succeeds and sets owner to the zero address.
Replaced _transferOwnership(newOwner) with _transferOwnership(_msgSender()) so ownership is always transferred to the caller instead of newOwner.
Replaced _transferOwnership(newOwner) with _transferOwnership(address(0)) so the owner is always set to the zero address.
Delete the require statement checking that newRoundImplementation is not the zero address, allowing the zero address to be stored.
Replace the assignment to roundImplementation with an assignment of the zero address, so the stored value is always 0x0.
Delete the statement that assigns newRoundImplementation to roundImplementation, so the state variable is never updated.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from updateRoundImplementation so any caller can set roundImplementation (whereas in P a non-owner call reverts, leaving the value unchanged).
Remove the _checkOwner() call from the onlyOwner modifier so any caller passes the guard and can change roundImplementation (in P, non-owner calls revert, leaving the value unchanged).
Delete the assignment `alloSettings = newAlloSettings;` so the state variable is never updated.
Replace the assignment with `alloSettings = address(0);` so updateAlloSettings always stores the zero address.
Replace the assignment with `alloSettings = roundImplementation;` so the stored value is the round implementation address instead of the parameter.
